supplemental_gap_fill.purpose: Exact first-party release/access/product chronology for material gaps not adequately reconstructed by present-day base indexes.

within_year_temporal_skew_audit.assessment: No catastrophic calendar hole. Q4 is densest and Q1 sparsest, but every month contains thousands of unique papers. Material completeness risk is dense-category query capping and historical publisher-index loss rather than an absent interval.

arxiv_cap_audit.assessment: Base arXiv success cannot establish exhaustive research coverage. Material annual anchors were checked by exact primary-source identity; residual non-headline omission risk remains explicit.

normalization_boundary.note: Repeated paper/announcement/availability observations are preserved as separate chronology evidence where objective state changes differ, while related observations are grouped into Evidence tasks for year-scale editorial reasoning.

residual_limitations: Present-day official indexes cannot prove that every 2022 publisher item remains linked or unchanged.
Ten capped arXiv month/category slices may omit non-headline research; targeted checks protect material editorial anchors but do not make the full research intake exhaustive.
The configured GitHub release watchlist returned no normalized 2022 release records and does not reconstruct commit-level runtime history exhaustively.
Some 2022 generative-media services and community projects have weak or mutable first-party archives; current absence is not treated as evidence of historical absence.
Vendor, project and author performance/capability claims remain attributed rather than treated as independently reproduced results.

single_volume_assessment.assessment: The reconstructed planes interact strongly enough to support a year-scale synthesis from steering/reasoning through compute/access, media distribution, code/action interfaces, and dialogue/evaluation/control. No evidence-backed need to split 2022 into H1/H2 is present.
